The step is also real and is the only part that can be done today: one transfer, one page, one call to ask what the actual number is. The chapter ends with the other half, care at the finish, for the day when the number is nearly done.
en.reminder: The road starts under your feet; keep the same care at its end.
en.acting: Do the one step that fits inside today: one payment, one page, one call.

zh_hant.plain: 債務、學位、房子的頭期款：數字大到讓人覺得開始也沒有用。
zh_hant.story:
靜的容易握住；還沒顯出來的容易計畫；脆的容易碎；小的容易散。在事情發生之前做；在混亂之前整理。合抱的樹，從細芽長出來；九層的台，從一筐土堆起來；千里的路，從腳下開始。強求的人毀了它；抓住的人失去它。人常在快成功時失敗；結尾和開始一樣小心，就沒有什麼會毀掉。

大數字會對人做一件事：整個一次到齊，身體就不肯動。這一章把整個和一步分開。整個是真的，而且一直是真的。這一步也是真的，而且是今天唯一做得到的那部分：一筆轉帳、一頁表、一通問清楚真正數字的電話。這一章以另一半結尾，結尾時的小心，留給數字快要完成的那一天。
zh_hant.reminder: 路從腳下開始；到結尾也留著同樣的小心。
zh_hant.acting: 做今天放得進去的那一步：一筆錢、一頁表、一通電話。

zh_hans.plain: 债务、学位、房子的头期款：数字大到让人觉得开始也没有用。
zh_hans.story:
静的容易握住；还没显出来的容易计划；脆的容易碎；小的容易散。在事情发生之前做；在混乱之前整理。合抱的树，从细芽长出来；九层的台，从一筐土堆起来；千里的路，从脚下开始。强求的人毁了它；抓住的人失去它。人常在快成功时失败；结尾和开始一样小心，就没有什么会毁掉。

大数字会对人做一件事：整个一次到齐，身体就不肯动。这一章把整个和一步分开。整个是真的，而且一直是真的。这一步也是真的，而且是今天唯一做得到的那部分：一笔转帐、一页表、一通问清楚真正数字的电话。这一章以另一半结尾，结尾时的小心，留给数字快要完成的那一天。
zh_hans.reminder: 路从脚下开始；到结尾也留着同样的小心。
zh_hans.acting: 做今天放得进去的那一步：一笔钱、一页表、一通电话。

lines: 古之善為道者非以明民
chapters.translation_en:
The ancients who showed their skill in practising the Tao did so, not to enlighten the people, but rather to make them simple and ignorant.
The difficulty in governing the people arises from their having much knowledge. He who (tries to) govern a state by his wisdom is a scourge to it; while he who does not (try to) do so is a blessing.
He who knows these two things finds in them also his model and rule. Ability to know this model and rule constitutes what we call the mysterious excellence (of a governor). Deep and far-reaching is such mysterious excellence, showing indeed its possessor as opposite to others, but leading them to a great conformity to him.

en.plain: You have been trying to outsmart a problem, the finances, a family conflict, and the cleverness is making it worse.
en.story:
Those of old who practised the way did not use it to make people clever but to keep them simple. People are hard to govern when they know too much. So governing by cleverness robs the state, and governing without it blesses the state. To know these two is to know the standard; to keep the standard always in mind is the deep virtue, deep and far, returning with all things to the great flow.

Laozi's suspicion of cleverness is not anti-intellectual. It is an observation about problems that get worse the more ingeniously they are handled. The financial scheme with seven moving parts. The family conflict managed by careful messaging. The chapter's word is simple, and the simple move is usually visible and unattractive: pay the plain amount, say the plain thing. It feels like giving up an advantage. It is giving up the complexity that was the problem's food.
en.reminder: Cleverness feeds the problem; the plain move starves it.
en.acting: Take the plain option on one tangled thing today, even though it looks like less.

zh_hant.plain: 你一直想用聰明智取一個問題，財務、家庭衝突，聰明讓它更糟。
zh_hant.story:
古時候行道的人，不用道讓人民聰明，而用它讓人民樸實。人民知道太多，就難治理。所以用聰明治國，是國的賊；不用聰明治國，是國的福。知道這兩個，就知道法則；一直記著這個法則，就是玄德，深而遠，跟萬物一起回到大順。

老子對聰明的懷疑不是反智。它是一個關於「越巧妙處理越糟」的問題的觀察。有七個活動零件的財務方案。靠小心措辭管理的家庭衝突。這一章的字是樸，而樸的那一步通常看得見、也不吸引人：付那個平實的數目，說那句平實的話。感覺像放棄了一個優勢。放棄的其實是那個問題賴以為食的複雜。
zh_hant.reminder: 聰明餵養問題；平實的那一步讓它餓。
zh_hant.acting: 今天對一件糾纏的事選那個平實的選項，就算它看起來比較少。

zh_hans.plain: 你一直想用聪明智取一个问题，财务、家庭冲突，聪明让它更糟。
zh_hans.story:
古时候行道的人，不用道让人民聪明，而用它让人民朴实。人民知道太多，就难治理。所以用聪明治国，是国的贼；不用聪明治国，是国的福。知道这两个，就知道法则；一直记着这个法则，就是玄德，深而远，跟万物一起回到大顺。

老子对聪明的怀疑不是反智。它是一个关于「越巧妙处理越糟」的问题的观察。有七个活动零件的财务方案。靠小心措辞管理的家庭冲突。这一章的字是朴，而朴的那一步通常看得见、也不吸引人：付那个平实的数目，说那句平实的话。感觉像放弃了一个优势。放弃的其实是那个问题赖以为食的复杂。
zh_hans.reminder: 聪明喂养问题；平实的那一步让它饿。
zh_hans.acting: 今天对一件纠缠的事选那个平实的选项，就算它看起来比较少。

lines: 江海所以能為百谷王者
以其善下之故能為百谷王
是以欲上民必以言下之
是以聖人處上而民不重
以其不爭故天下莫能與之爭
chapters.translation_en:
That whereby the rivers and seas are able to receive the homage and tribute of all the valley streams, is their skill in being lower than they;--it is thus that they are the kings of them all. So it is that the sage (ruler), wishing to be above men, puts himself by his words below them, and, wishing to be before them, places his person behind them.
In this way though he has his place above them, men do not feel his weight, nor though he has his place before them, do they feel it an injury to them.
Therefore all in the world delight to exalt him and do not weary of him. Because he does not strive, no one finds it possible to strive with him.

en.plain: You lead people, at work or in a group, and lately they follow reluctantly.
en.story:
Rivers and seas are kings of the valleys because they are good at staying below them. So to be above people, the sage speaks from below; to be ahead, stays behind. Then people carry the sage above without feeling the weight, and ahead without feeling harmed. The whole world is glad to lift such a person and never tires of it, because there is no contending, and so nobody contends.

Reluctant following is the feeling of weight. People carry a leader who is above them and it costs them; they lift a leader who speaks from below and it costs nothing. The chapter's method is specific: put yourself behind and below in the conversation. Ask before telling. Take the smaller share. Credit the group in front of the group. None of it reduces the leader's position; it removes the weight that made the position hard to carry.
en.reminder: Lead from below and nobody feels the weight.
en.acting: In the next meeting, speak last, and give the first credit to someone else.

zh_hant.plain: 你帶著人，公司裡或一個團體裡，最近他們跟得很勉強。
zh_hant.story:
江海是百谷的王，因為它善於待在它們的下面。所以要在人上面，聖人說話從下面說；要在前面，就待在後面。這樣人們把聖人抬在上面而不覺得重，放在前面而不覺得受害。天下樂於推舉這樣的人而不厭倦，因為他不爭，所以沒有人跟他爭。

勉強的跟隨，是感覺到重量。人們抬一個在他們上面的領導者，是有代價的；他們抬一個從下面說話的領導者，不花什麼。這一章的方法很具體：在對話裡把自己放到後面和下面。先問再說。拿小的那一份。在團體面前把功勞給團體。這些都不減少領導者的位置；它們拿掉的是讓位置難以被抬起的重量。
zh_hant.reminder: 從下面帶，沒有人覺得重。
zh_hant.acting: 下一次會議最後一個說話，把第一份功勞給別人。

zh_hans.plain: 你带着人，公司里或一个团体里，最近他们跟得很勉强。
zh_hans.story:
江海是百谷的王，因为它善于待在它们的下面。所以要在人上面，圣人说话从下面说；要在前面，就待在后面。这样人们把圣人擡在上面而不觉得重，放在前面而不觉得受害。天下乐于推举这样的人而不厌倦，因为他不争，所以没有人跟他争。

勉强的跟随，是感觉到重量。人们擡一个在他们上面的领导者，是有代价的；他们擡一个从下面说话的领导者，不花什么。这一章的方法很具体：在对话里把自己放到后面和下面。先问再说。拿小的那一份。在团体面前把功劳给团体。这些都不减少领导者的位置；它们拿掉的是让位置难以被擡起的重量。
zh_hans.reminder: 从下面带，没有人觉得重。
zh_hans.acting: 下一次会议最后一个说话，把第一份功劳给别人。

lines: 天下皆謂我道大似不肖
不敢為天下先故能成器長
舍儉且廣舍後且先死矣
chapters.translation_en:
All the world says that, while my Tao is great, it yet appears to be inferior (to other systems of teaching). Now it is just its greatness that makes it seem to be inferior. If it were like any other (system), for long would its smallness have been known!
But I have three precious things which I prize and hold fast. The first is gentleness; the second is economy; and the third is shrinking from taking precedence of others.
With that gentleness I can be bold; with that economy I can be liberal; shrinking from taking precedence of others, I can become a vessel of the highest honour. Now-a-days they give up gentleness and are all for being bold; economy, and are all for being liberal; the hindmost place, and seek only to be foremost;--(of all which the end is) death.
Gentleness is sure to be victorious even in battle, and firmly to maintain its ground. Heaven will save its possessor, by his (very) gentleness protecting him.

en.plain: You are being told to be tougher, bolder, more ambitious, and it is against your grain.
en.story:
Everyone says my way is great and unlike anything, Laozi says; it is great because it is unlike anything. I have three treasures: compassion, frugality, and not daring to be first in the world. Compassion makes courage possible; frugality makes generosity possible; not daring to be first makes leadership possible. Courage without compassion, generosity without frugality, leading without staying behind: these are death. Compassion wins in attack and holds in defence; heaven arms with compassion those it would save.

The chapter is a direct answer to advice about being tougher. Laozi's courage comes from compassion, not from the absence of it. His generosity comes from having kept something back. His leadership comes from not needing to be first. A person told to go against their grain can check which grain: if it is one of these three, it is the treasure, and the advice is to spend it.
en.reminder: Courage grows from compassion, not against it.
en.acting: Do one brave thing today in your own style: the kind that starts from care rather than from force.

zh_hant.plain: 有人要你更強硬、更大膽、更有野心，而這違背你的本性。
zh_hant.story:
老子說，人人都說我的道大，不像任何東西；它大，正因為它不像任何東西。我有三件寶：慈，儉，不敢為天下先。慈讓勇成為可能；儉讓廣成為可能；不敢為先讓領導成為可能。沒有慈的勇，沒有儉的廣，不留在後面的領導：這些是死。慈，攻能勝，守能固；天要救誰，就用慈來武裝他。

這一章是對「要更強硬」這類建議的直接回答。老子的勇來自慈，不是來自沒有慈。他的廣來自留了一些。他的領導來自不需要當第一。被要求違背本性的人可以檢查是哪一種本性：如果是這三件之一，那就是寶，而建議是把它花出去。
zh_hant.reminder: 勇從慈長出來，不是逆著慈。
zh_hant.acting: 今天用你自己的方式做一件勇敢的事：從關心出發的那一種，不是從力量出發。

zh_hans.plain: 有人要你更强硬、更大胆、更有野心，而这违背你的本性。
zh_hans.story:
老子说，人人都说我的道大，不像任何东西；它大，正因为它不像任何东西。我有三件宝：慈，俭，不敢为天下先。慈让勇成为可能；俭让广成为可能；不敢为先让领导成为可能。没有慈的勇，没有俭的广，不留在后面的领导：这些是死。慈，攻能胜，守能固；天要救谁，就用慈来武装他。

这一章是对「要更强硬」这类建议的直接回答。老子的勇来自慈，不是来自没有慈。他的广来自留了一些。他的领导来自不需要当第一。被要求违背本性的人可以检查是哪一种本性：如果是这三件之一，那就是宝，而建议是把它花出去。
zh_hans.reminder: 勇从慈长出来，不是逆着慈。
zh_hans.acting: 今天用你自己的方式做一件勇敢的事：从关心出发的那一种，不是从力量出发。

lines: 是謂不爭之德是謂用人之力
chapters.translation_en:
He who in (Tao's) wars has skill
 Assumes no martial port;
 He who fights with most good will
 To rage makes no resort.
 He who vanquishes yet still
 Keeps from his foes apart;
 He whose hests men most fulfil
 Yet humbly plies his art.
 Thus we say, 'He ne'er contends,
 And therein is his might.'
 Thus we say, 'Men's wills he bends,
 That they with him unite.'
 Thus we say, 'Like Heaven's his ends,
 No sage of old more bright.'

en.plain: A rival at work keeps escalating, and you are wondering whether to fight back at the same pitch.
en.story:
The good soldier is not warlike; the good fighter is not angry; the good winner does not engage; the good employer of people puts himself below them. This is called the virtue of not contending, the use of others' strength, matching heaven, the highest of the ancient ways.

The chapter is about winning without engaging, and it is not about weakness. The good fighter is not angry because anger is what the rival's escalation is designed to produce. The good winner does not engage because the engagement is the rival's home ground. What is left is quiet competence, done where it can be seen, with the rival's energy left to spend itself. This does not always win. It always costs less, and it leaves you as someone the rest of the office can work with afterwards.
en.reminder: Do not fight at their pitch; let their energy spend itself.
en.acting: Do the piece of work that speaks for you this week, and answer the rival with nothing at all.

zh_hant.plain: 公司裡一個對手不斷升高衝突，你在想要不要用同樣的調子反擊。
zh_hant.story:
好的軍人不好戰；好的鬥士不發怒；好的勝者不交手；好的用人者把自己放在人下面。這叫不爭的德，叫用別人的力，叫配天，是古代最高的道。

這一章講的是不交手而勝，它不是關於軟弱。好的鬥士不發怒，因為發怒正是對手升高衝突想製造的東西。好的勝者不交手，因為交手是對手的主場。剩下的是安靜的本事，做在看得見的地方，讓對手的力氣自己花掉。這不一定每次都贏。它每次都花費比較少，而且事後你還是辦公室裡其他人願意合作的那個人。
zh_hant.reminder: 不用他們的調子打；讓他們的力氣自己花掉。
zh_hant.acting: 這星期做那件替你說話的工作，對那個對手什麼也不回。

zh_hans.plain: 公司里一个对手不断升高冲突，你在想要不要用同样的调子反击。
zh_hans.story:
好的军人不好战；好的斗士不发怒；好的胜者不交手；好的用人者把自己放在人下面。这叫不争的德，叫用别人的力，叫配天，是古代最高的道。

这一章讲的是不交手而胜，它不是关于软弱。好的斗士不发怒，因为发怒正是对手升高冲突想制造的东西。好的胜者不交手，因为交手是对手的主场。剩下的是安静的本事，做在看得见的地方，让对手的力气自己花掉。这不一定每次都赢。它每次都花费比较少，而且事后你还是办公室里其他人愿意合作的那个人。
zh_hans.reminder: 不用他们的调子打；让他们的力气自己花掉。
zh_hans.acting: 这星期做那件替你说话的工作，对那个对手什么也不回。

lines: 用兵有言吾不敢為主而為客
禍莫大於輕敵輕敵幾喪吾寶
chapters.translation_en:
A master of the art of war has said, 'I do not dare to be the host (to commence the war); I prefer to be the guest (to act on the defensive). I do not dare to advance an inch; I prefer to retire a foot.' This is called marshalling the ranks where there are no ranks; baring the arms (to fight) where there are no arms to bare; grasping the weapon where there is no weapon to grasp; advancing against the enemy where there is no enemy.
There is no calamity greater than lightly engaging in war. To do that is near losing (the gentleness) which is so precious. Thus it is that when opposing weapons are (actually) crossed, he who deplores (the situation) conquers.

en.plain: You are about to go into a negotiation, over pay, over a lease, over a family matter, and you feel outgunned.
en.story:
The strategists say: I dare not be the host but the guest; I dare not advance an inch but retreat a foot. This is called marching without moving, rolling up sleeves without arms, holding without weapons, opposing without an enemy. No disaster is greater than underestimating the opponent; underestimating nearly costs my treasures. So when matched forces meet, the side that grieves wins.

The advice is for the weaker side, and the weaker side is where most negotiations are felt from. Be the guest: let the other party set out their position first. Retreat a foot: concede the small thing early and cheaply. Do not underestimate them, which is the only real error. And the last line is the strangest and most useful: the side that grieves wins. The one who goes in knowing what they stand to lose is more careful, more patient, and harder to move than the one who goes in confident.
en.reminder: Be the guest; grieve first; do not underestimate them.
en.acting: Before the negotiation, write down the one thing you cannot give up and the two you can.

zh_hant.plain: 你就要進入一場談判，談薪水、談租約、談一件家裡的事，你覺得火力不如人。
zh_hant.story:
兵法家說：我不敢做主人而做客人；不敢進一寸而退一尺。這叫不動而行軍，沒有手臂而捲袖，沒有兵器而握持，沒有敵人而對抗。沒有比輕視對手更大的災禍；輕視對手，幾乎讓我失去三寶。所以勢均力敵時，哀傷的一邊贏。

這是給弱勢一方的建議，而弱勢一方正是多數談判被感覺到的位置。做客人：讓對方先擺出立場。退一尺：早早地、便宜地讓出小的東西。不要輕視他們，那是唯一真正的錯。最後一句最奇怪也最有用：哀傷的一邊贏。知道自己會失去什麼而進去的人，比帶著自信進去的人更小心、更有耐心、更難被推動。
zh_hant.reminder: 做客人；先哀；不要輕視他們。
zh_hant.acting: 談判之前，寫下你不能讓的那一樣東西，和可以讓的兩樣。

zh_hans.plain: 你就要进入一场谈判，谈薪水、谈租约、谈一件家里的事，你觉得火力不如人。
zh_hans.story:
兵法家说：我不敢做主人而做客人；不敢进一寸而退一尺。这叫不动而行军，没有手臂而卷袖，没有兵器而握持，没有敌人而对抗。没有比轻视对手更大的灾祸；轻视对手，几乎让我失去三宝。所以势均力敌时，哀伤的一边赢。

这是给弱势一方的建议，而弱势一方正是多数谈判被感觉到的位置。做客人：让对方先摆出立场。退一尺：早早地、便宜地让出小的东西。不要轻视他们，那是唯一真正的错。最后一句最奇怪也最有用：哀伤的一边赢。知道自己会失去什么而进去的人，比带着自信进去的人更小心、更有耐心、更难被推动。
zh_hans.reminder: 做客人；先哀；不要轻视他们。
zh_hans.acting: 谈判之前，写下你不能让的那一样东西，和可以让的两样。

chapters.translation_en:
My words are very easy to know, and very easy to practise; but there is no one in the world who is able to know and able to practise them.
There is an originating and all-comprehending (principle) in my words, and an authoritative law for the things (which I enforce). It is because they do not know these, that men do not know me.
They who know me are few, and I am on that account (the more) to be prized. It is thus that the sage wears (a poor garb of) hair cloth, while he carries his (signet of) jade in his bosom.

en.plain: You explain yourself carefully and people still do not get it, and you have started to feel invisible.
en.story:
My words are very easy to understand and very easy to practise, Laozi says, yet no one under heaven understands or practises them. Words have an ancestor; deeds have a master; because people do not know these, they do not know me. Those who know me are few, and so I am prized. The sage wears coarse cloth and carries jade inside.

The chapter is the author admitting he is not understood, and the tone is not bitter. He does not shout louder or explain again. He keeps the jade inside the coarse cloth and lets the few who can see it, see it. For someone tired of explaining themselves, the chapter is permission to stop: the explanation was never what made the thing true, and the people who need to see it usually do without the speech. Wear the coarse cloth. Do the work. The jade is not less jade for being unseen.
en.reminder: Coarse cloth outside; jade inside; stop explaining.
en.acting: Leave the explanation out once today and let the work speak; note who understands anyway.

zh_hant.plain: 你小心地解釋自己，別人還是不懂，你開始覺得自己是隱形的。
zh_hant.story:
老子說，我的話很容易懂，很容易做，天下卻沒有人懂、沒有人做。話有祖宗；事有主人；因為人們不知道這些，所以不知道我。知道我的人少，所以我珍貴。聖人穿粗布，懷裡揣著玉。

這一章是作者承認自己不被理解，語氣不苦。他沒有喊得更大聲，也沒有再解釋一次。他把玉留在粗布裡面，讓少數看得見的人看見。對一個厭倦了解釋自己的人，這一章是停下來的許可：解釋從來就不是讓那件事為真的東西，而需要看見它的人，通常不用那番話也看得見。穿粗布。做事。玉不會因為沒被看見就不是玉。
zh_hant.reminder: 外面粗布；裡面是玉；別再解釋。
zh_hant.acting: 今天少解釋一次，讓工作說話；注意誰照樣懂了。

zh_hans.plain: 你小心地解释自己，别人还是不懂，你开始觉得自己是隐形的。
zh_hans.story:
老子说，我的话很容易懂，很容易做，天下却没有人懂、没有人做。话有祖宗；事有主人；因为人们不知道这些，所以不知道我。知道我的人少，所以我珍贵。圣人穿粗布，怀里揣着玉。

这一章是作者承认自己不被理解，语气不苦。他没有喊得更大声，也没有再解释一次。他把玉留在粗布里面，让少数看得见的人看见。对一个厌倦了解释自己的人，这一章是停下来的许可：解释从来就不是让那件事为真的东西，而需要看见它的人，通常不用那番话也看得见。穿粗布。做事。玉不会因为没被看见就不是玉。
zh_hans.reminder: 外面粗布；里面是玉；别再解释。
zh_hans.acting: 今天少解释一次，让工作说话；注意谁照样懂了。

lines: 聖人不病以其病病是以不病
chapters.translation_en:
To know and yet (think) we do not know is the highest (attainment); not to know (and yet think) we do know is a disease.
It is simply by being pained at (the thought of) having this disease that we are preserved from it. The sage has not the disease.
He knows the pain that would be inseparable from it, and therefore he does not have it.

en.plain: You are expected to have the answer, at work, at home, and admitting you do not feels dangerous.
en.story:
To know that you do not know is best. To think you know when you do not is a sickness. Only by being sick of this sickness is one free of it. The sage is free of it because he is sick of it.

The chapter is four lines and it is about the pressure to have the answer. The person who says I do not know yet in a meeting is doing the highest thing in the chapter, and it rarely feels that way. The sickness Laozi names is the other thing: the confident answer given because silence felt dangerous, which then has to be defended. Knowing where your knowledge ends is a skill, and the people worth working with recognise it. Say the true thing: I will find out.
en.reminder: I do not know yet is the best thing to know.
en.acting: Say I do not know once today where you would usually guess, and then go and find out.

zh_hant.plain: 大家期待你有答案，公司裡、家裡，承認自己不知道感覺很危險。
zh_hant.story:
知道自己不知道，最好。不知道卻以為知道，是病。只有把這種病當病，才不會有病。聖人沒有病，因為他把病當病。

這一章四句，講的是「必須有答案」的壓力。在會議上說「我還不知道」的人，做的是這一章裡最高的事，而它很少讓人這樣覺得。老子叫做病的是另一件事：因為沉默感覺危險而給出的自信答案，然後還得去守它。知道自己的知識到哪裡為止是一種本事，值得共事的人認得它。說真話：我去查。
zh_hant.reminder: 「我還不知道」，是最好的知道。
zh_hant.acting: 今天在你通常會猜的地方說一次「我不知道」，然後去弄清楚。

zh_hans.plain: 大家期待你有答案，公司里、家里，承认自己不知道感觉很危险。
zh_hans.story:
知道自己不知道，最好。不知道却以为知道，是病。只有把这种病当病，才不会有病。圣人没有病，因为他把病当病。

这一章四句，讲的是「必须有答案」的压力。在会议上说「我还不知道」的人，做的是这一章里最高的事，而它很少让人这样觉得。老子叫做病的是另一件事：因为沉默感觉危险而给出的自信答案，然后还得去守它。知道自己的知识到哪里为止是一种本事，值得共事的人认得它。说真话：我去查。
zh_hans.reminder: 「我还不知道」，是最好的知道。
zh_hans.acting: 今天在你通常会猜的地方说一次「我不知道」，然后去弄清楚。

lines: 無狎其所居無厭其所生
chapters.translation_en:
When the people do not fear what they ought to fear, that which is their great dread will come on them.
Let them not thoughtlessly indulge themselves in their ordinary life; let them not act as if weary of what that life depends on.
It is by avoiding such indulgence that such weariness does not arise.
Therefore the sage knows (these things) of himself, but does not parade (his knowledge); loves, but does not (appear to set a) value on, himself. And thus he puts the latter alternative away and makes choice of the former.

en.plain: Everything feels like a threat lately, the email from the boss, the letter from the bank, and you are worn down by bracing.
en.story:
When people do not fear what should be feared, something greater arrives. Do not narrow their dwellings; do not weary them of their lives. Only by not wearying them are they not wearied. So the sage knows himself without displaying, loves himself without exalting, and lets go of the one to take the other.

The chapter is about a person worn down by being made to fear, and its counsel is oddly tender: love yourself without exalting yourself. The bracing against every email is a kind of self-narrowing, a life lived in a smaller room than necessary. Most of the feared things are not the greater thing the chapter warns of; they are letters, and letters can be opened. Widen the dwelling. Open the letter, and see the size of what is actually there.
en.reminder: Open the letter; it is usually smaller than the bracing.
en.acting: Open the one message you have been avoiding today, and write down its actual size in one line.

zh_hant.plain: 最近什麼都像威脅，老闆的信、銀行的信，你被繃緊磨損了。
zh_hant.story:
當人民不怕該怕的東西，更大的東西就來了。不要逼窄他們住的地方；不要讓他們厭倦自己的生活。只有不讓他們厭倦，他們才不厭倦。所以聖人知道自己而不顯示，愛自己而不抬高，捨去那一個，取這一個。

這一章講的是被弄得害怕而磨損的人，它的建議奇怪地溫柔：愛自己，而不抬高自己。對每一封信的繃緊，是一種把自己逼窄的方式，活在一個比需要小的房間裡。多數害怕的東西不是這一章警告的那個更大的東西；它們是信，而信可以打開。把住的地方拓寬。打開那封信，看看真正在那裡的東西有多大。
zh_hant.reminder: 打開那封信；它通常比繃緊小。
zh_hant.acting: 今天打開你一直在避開的那則訊息，用一行寫下它真正的大小。

zh_hans.plain: 最近什么都像威胁，老板的信、银行的信，你被绷紧磨损了。
zh_hans.story:
当人民不怕该怕的东西，更大的东西就来了。不要逼窄他们住的地方；不要让他们厌倦自己的生活。只有不让他们厌倦，他们才不厌倦。所以圣人知道自己而不显示，爱自己而不擡高，舍去那一个，取这一个。

这一章讲的是被弄得害怕而磨损的人，它的建议奇怪地温柔：爱自己，而不擡高自己。对每一封信的绷紧，是一种把自己逼窄的方式，活在一个比需要小的房间里。多数害怕的东西不是这一章警告的那个更大的东西；它们是信，而信可以打开。把住的地方拓宽。打开那封信，看看真正在那里的东西有多大。
zh_hans.reminder: 打开那封信；它通常比绷紧小。
zh_hans.acting: 今天打开你一直在避开的那则消息，用一行写下它真正的大小。

chapters.translation_en:
He whose boldness appears in his daring (to do wrong, in defiance of the laws) is put to death; he whose boldness appears in his not daring (to do so) lives on. Of these two cases the one appears to be advantageous, and the other to be injurious. But
 When Heaven's anger smites a man,
 Who the cause shall truly scan?
On this account the sage feels a difficulty (as to what to do in the former case).
It is the way of Heaven not to strive, and yet it skilfully overcomes; not to speak, and yet it is skilful in obtaining a reply; does not call, and yet men come to it of themselves. Its demonstrations are quiet, and yet its plans are skilful and effective.
The meshes of the net of Heaven are large; far apart, but letting nothing escape.

en.plain: Someone got away with something at your expense, and you want to see them pay for it.
en.story:
Bold in daring, one is killed; bold in not daring, one lives. Of these two, one benefits and one harms; who knows why heaven dislikes what it dislikes? The way of heaven does not contend and yet wins, does not speak and yet is answered, is not summoned and yet arrives, is unhurried and yet plans well. Heaven's net is vast, wide-meshed, and loses nothing.

The last line is the one people remember, and it is meant for exactly this situation. The person who got away with it has not left the net; the net is wide and slow, and it loses nothing. The chapter's practical advice is in the middle: do not contend, do not summon, do not press. Pursuing the payment yourself is the bold daring that harms. Let the net do what it does, and turn your own hands to work that is yours.
en.reminder: The net is wide and slow, and it loses nothing.
en.acting: Write down what you would have done to make them pay, then do the opposite: one hour of your own work instead.

zh_hant.plain: 有人在你的代價上逃過了，你想看他付出代價。
zh_hant.story:
勇於敢，就被殺；勇於不敢，就活。這兩種，一個有利一個有害；天所厭惡的，誰知道為什麼？天的道不爭而勝，不說而有回應，不召喚而自己來，不急而計畫得好。天網恢恢，疏而不失。

最後一句是人們記得的那一句，而它正是為這種處境說的。逃過的那個人沒有離開網；網又寬又慢，而且什麼都不漏。這一章實際的建議在中間：不爭，不召喚，不逼。自己去追那份代價，是那種有害的勇於敢。讓網做它做的事，把自己的手轉回屬於你的工作。
zh_hant.reminder: 網又寬又慢，什麼都不漏。
zh_hant.acting: 寫下你本來想怎麼讓他付出代價，然後做相反的：改做一個小時自己的工作。

zh_hans.plain: 有人在你的代价上逃过了，你想看他付出代价。
zh_hans.story:
勇于敢，就被杀；勇于不敢，就活。这两种，一个有利一个有害；天所厌恶的，谁知道为什么？天的道不争而胜，不说而有回应，不召唤而自己来，不急而计划得好。天网恢恢，疏而不失。

最后一句是人们记得的那一句，而它正是为这种处境说的。逃过的那个人没有离开网；网又宽又慢，而且什么都不漏。这一章实际的建议在中间：不争，不召唤，不逼。自己去追那份代价，是那种有害的勇于敢。让网做它做的事，把自己的手转回属于你的工作。
zh_hans.reminder: 网又宽又慢，什么都不漏。
zh_hans.acting: 写下你本来想怎么让他付出代价，然后做相反的：改做一个小时自己的工作。

lines: 民不畏死奈何以死懼之
若使民常畏死而為奇者
常有司殺者殺夫代司殺者殺
chapters.translation_en:
The people do not fear death; to what purpose is it to (try to) frighten them with death? If the people were always in awe of death, and I could always seize those who do wrong, and put them to death, who would dare to do wrong?
There is always One who presides over the infliction of death. He who would inflict death in the room of him who so presides over it may be described as hewing wood instead of a great carpenter. Seldom is it that he who undertakes the hewing, instead of the great carpenter, does not cut his own hands!

en.plain: You have been threatening consequences, to a child, a tenant, a team, and the threats have stopped working.
en.story:
If people do not fear death, what use is threatening them with it? And if they did fear it, and we seized and killed the wrongdoers, who would dare? There is always the executioner who does the killing; to do it in his place is to hew wood for the master carpenter, and few who do that escape cutting their own hands.

The chapter is about the limits of threat, and it is addressed to whoever has been using it. Consequences that have stopped working have stopped because the person no longer fears them, and raising the stakes only proves it. Laozi's image is the amateur with the master carpenter's axe: it is not that punishment never has a place, but that taking it into your own hands cuts you. Set the axe aside. Say what will happen once, without heat, and let the situation carry its own consequences.
en.reminder: Put down the master carpenter's axe.
en.acting: Replace the next threat with a plain statement of what will happen, said once, without raising your voice.

zh_hant.plain: 你一直在威脅後果，對孩子、房客、團隊，威脅已經不管用了。
zh_hant.story:
人民若不怕死，拿死威脅他們有什麼用？如果他們怕死，我們抓來殺掉作惡的人，誰還敢？總有那個負責殺的行刑者；代替他去殺，就像替大木匠砍木頭，替大木匠砍木頭的人，很少不砍傷自己的手。

這一章講的是威脅的極限，對象是一直在用威脅的人。不管用的後果，是因為對方不再怕了，再加碼只是證明這件事。老子的畫面是拿著大木匠斧頭的外行人：不是懲罰永遠沒有位置，而是把它拿到自己手裡，會砍到自己。把那把斧頭擱到一邊。把會發生什麼說一次，不帶火氣，讓處境自己承擔它的後果。
zh_hant.reminder: 把大木匠的斧頭擱到一邊。
zh_hant.acting: 把下一次威脅換成一句平實的「會發生什麼」，說一次，不提高聲音。

zh_hans.plain: 你一直在威胁后果，对孩子、房客、团队，威胁已经不管用了。
zh_hans.story:
人民若不怕死，拿死威胁他们有什么用？如果他们怕死，我们抓来杀掉作恶的人，谁还敢？总有那个负责杀的行刑者；代替他去杀，就像替大木匠砍木头，替大木匠砍木头的人，很少不砍伤自己的手。

这一章讲的是威胁的极限，对象是一直在用威胁的人。不管用的后果，是因为对方不再怕了，再加码只是证明这件事。老子的画面是拿着大木匠斧头的外行人：不是惩罚永远没有位置，而是把它拿到自己手里，会砍到自己。把那把斧头搁到一边。把会发生什么说一次，不带火气，让处境自己承担它的后果。
zh_hans.reminder: 把大木匠的斧头搁到一边。
zh_hans.acting: 把下一次威胁换成一句平实的「会发生什么」，说一次，不提高声音。

lines: 民之饑以其上食稅之多
民之難治以其上之有為
民之輕死以其上求生之厚
夫唯無以生為者是賢於貴生
chapters.translation_en:
The people suffer from famine because of the multitude of taxes consumed by their superiors. It is through this that they suffer famine.
The people are difficult to govern because of the (excessive) agency of their superiors (in governing them). It is through this that they are difficult to govern.
The people make light of dying because of the greatness of their labours in seeking for the means of living. It is this which makes them think light of dying. Thus it is that to leave the subject of living altogether out of view is better than to set a high value on it.

en.plain: The cost of everything keeps rising, and you feel squeezed from above by people who do not seem to feel it.
en.story:
The people are hungry because those above eat too much in taxes; that is why they are hungry. The people are hard to govern because those above interfere; that is why they are hard to govern. The people make light of death because those above pursue life too intensely; that is why they make light of death. Only one who does not strive to live is wiser than one who prizes life.

This is the chapter that says out loud what the squeezed person already knows: the pressure comes from above, and it is not their doing. Laozi is not offering a remedy for the taxes; he is refusing to let the hunger be blamed on the hungry. For the person reading it on a hard month, that is the use: the squeeze is real, it has a source, and the source is not a flaw in you. The last line is the only advice, and it is for the squeezed, not the squeezers: do not add to the pressure by striving to match them.
en.reminder: The squeeze has a source, and the source is not you.
en.acting: Cut one expense that exists only to keep up with people above you, and keep the money.

zh_hant.plain: 什麼都在漲，你覺得被上面那些好像沒有感覺的人擠壓。
zh_hant.story:
人民餓，是因為上面的人吃太多稅；所以他們餓。人民難治理，是因為上面的人干擾；所以他們難治理。人民輕視死，是因為上面的人太用力地求活；所以他們輕視死。只有不用力求活的人，比看重活的人更有智慧。

這一章把被擠壓的人早就知道的事大聲說出來：壓力來自上面，不是他們造成的。老子沒有給稅的解方；他拒絕讓餓被怪到餓的人身上。對一個在艱難月份讀它的人，用處就在這裡：擠壓是真的，它有來源，而來源不是你身上的缺陷。最後一句是唯一的建議，而它是給被擠的人，不是給擠的人：不要為了跟上他們而給自己加壓。
zh_hant.reminder: 擠壓有來源，來源不是你。
zh_hant.acting: 砍掉一項只為了跟上上面的人而存在的開銷，把錢留著。

zh_hans.plain: 什么都在涨，你觉得被上面那些好像没有感觉的人挤压。
zh_hans.story:
人民饿，是因为上面的人吃太多税；所以他们饿。人民难治理，是因为上面的人干扰；所以他们难治理。人民轻视死，是因为上面的人太用力地求活；所以他们轻视死。只有不用力求活的人，比看重活的人更有智能。

这一章把被挤压的人早就知道的事大声说出来：压力来自上面，不是他们造成的。老子没有给税的解方；他拒绝让饿被怪到饿的人身上。对一个在艰难月份读它的人，用处就在这里：挤压是真的，它有来源，而来源不是你身上的缺陷。最后一句是唯一的建议，而它是给被挤的人，不是给挤的人：不要为了跟上他们而给自己加压。
zh_hans.reminder: 挤压有来源，来源不是你。
zh_hans.acting: 砍掉一项只为了跟上上面的人而存在的开销，把钱留着。

lines: 人之生也柔弱其死也堅強
chapters.translation_en:
Man at his birth is supple and weak; at his death, firm and strong. (So it is with) all things. Trees and plants, in their early growth, are soft and brittle; at their death, dry and withered.
Thus it is that firmness and strength are the concomitants of death; softness and weakness, the concomitants of life.
Hence he who (relies on) the strength of his forces does not conquer; and a tree which is strong will fill the out-stretched arms, (and thereby invites the feller.)
Therefore the place of what is firm and strong is below, and that of what is soft and weak is above.

en.plain: You have made yourself hard to survive a hard year, and now you cannot soften even when it is safe.
en.story:
A person alive is soft and yielding; dead, hard and stiff. Plants alive are soft and pliant; dead, dry and brittle. So the hard and stiff are companions of death; the soft and yielding, companions of life. An army that is rigid does not win; a tree that is rigid is felled. The hard and great sits below; the soft and weak sits above.

The chapter's evidence is biological, and it applies to a person who armoured up to survive. The armour worked. The chapter only observes what armour is made of: the hard and stiff, which is the texture of what has stopped growing. Softening again is not a return to vulnerability; it is a return to being alive in the way a green branch is, able to bend when the wind comes rather than snapping. Start where it is safe: at home, with one person, one evening.
en.reminder: Soft is what alive feels like.
en.acting: Let one guard down this evening with one safe person, and notice that you are still here afterwards.

zh_hant.plain: 為了撐過艱難的一年，你把自己變硬了，現在就算安全了也軟不下來。
zh_hant.story:
人活著的時候柔軟，死了就僵硬。草木活著的時候柔韌，死了就乾脆。所以堅硬的是死的同伴；柔軟的是生的同伴。軍隊僵硬就不會贏；樹僵硬就被砍。硬而大的在下面；柔而弱的在上面。

這一章的證據是生物學的，它適用於為了活下來而穿上盔甲的人。盔甲有用。這一章只是觀察盔甲是什麼做的：硬和僵，那是停止生長的東西的質地。再軟下來不是回到脆弱；是回到像一根綠枝那樣活著，風來的時候能彎，而不是斷。從安全的地方開始：家裡，一個人，一個晚上。
zh_hant.reminder: 軟，就是活著的感覺。
zh_hant.acting: 今晚對一個安全的人卸下一道防備，然後注意，你之後還在。

zh_hans.plain: 为了撑过艰难的一年，你把自己变硬了，现在就算安全了也软不下来。
zh_hans.story:
人活着的时候柔软，死了就僵硬。草木活着的时候柔韧，死了就干脆。所以坚硬的是死的同伴；柔软的是生的同伴。军队僵硬就不会赢；树僵硬就被砍。硬而大的在下面；柔而弱的在上面。

这一章的证据是生物学的，它适用于为了活下来而穿上盔甲的人。盔甲有用。这一章只是观察盔甲是什么做的：硬和僵，那是停止生长的东西的质地。再软下来不是回到脆弱；是回到像一根绿枝那样活着，风来的时候能弯，而不是断。从安全的地方开始：家里，一个人，一个晚上。
zh_hans.reminder: 软，就是活着的感觉。
zh_hans.acting: 今晚对一个安全的人卸下一道防备，然后注意，你之后还在。

lines: 有餘者損之不足者補之
天之道損有餘而補不足
功成而不處其不欲見賢
chapters.translation_en:
May not the Way (or Tao) of Heaven be compared to the (method of) bending a bow? The (part of the bow) which was high is brought low, and what was low is raised up. (So Heaven) diminishes where there is superabundance, and supplements where there is deficiency.
It is the Way of Heaven to diminish superabundance, and to supplement deficiency. It is not so with the way of man. He takes away from those who have not enough to add to his own superabundance.
Who can take his own superabundance and therewith serve all under heaven? Only he who is in possession of the Tao!
Therefore the (ruling) sage acts without claiming the results as his; he achieves his merit and does not rest (arrogantly) in it:--he does not wish to display his superiority.

en.plain: The gap between what you earn and what others earn for the same work is wide, and it is hard not to be bitter.
en.story:
The way of heaven is like drawing a bow: the high end is pressed down, the low end raised, the excess taken, the deficient supplied. Heaven's way takes from what has too much and gives to what has too little. The human way is otherwise: it takes from those who have too little to add to those who have too much. Who can give their surplus to the world? Only one who has the way.

Laozi states the injustice flatly, which is more than most consolations do: the human way takes from the poor to give to the rich. He does not say it is fair. He says heaven's way is otherwise, and that a person can choose which way to practise in their own small economy. The bitterness is honest and it has a use, if it becomes the reason you take the bow's stance yourself: press the high end down where you have any say, and raise the low end where you can.
en.reminder: The human way is unjust; you can still draw the bow the other way.
en.acting: Give one hour, one skill or one introduction this week to someone who has less than you.

zh_hant.plain: 你和別人做同樣的工作，收入的差距很大，很難不苦澀。
zh_hant.story:
天的道像拉弓：高的一端壓下來，低的一端抬起來，多的拿掉，少的補上。天的道，從有餘的拿走，給不足的。人的道不一樣：從不足的拿走，加給有餘的。誰能把自己的餘給天下？只有有道的人。

老子把不公平平平地說出來，這比多數安慰做得多：人的道從窮人拿走給富人。他沒有說這公平。他說天的道不一樣，而一個人可以在自己小小的經濟裡選擇練哪一種道。苦澀是誠實的，它有用處，如果它變成你自己擺出拉弓姿勢的理由：在你說得上話的地方把高的一端壓下來，在你做得到的地方把低的一端抬起來。
zh_hant.reminder: 人的道不公平；你仍然可以反過來拉這張弓。
zh_hant.acting: 這星期給一個比你少的人一個小時、一項本事、或一次引介。

zh_hans.plain: 你和别人做同样的工作，收入的差距很大，很难不苦涩。
zh_hans.story:
天的道像拉弓：高的一端压下来，低的一端擡起来，多的拿掉，少的补上。天的道，从有余的拿走，给不足的。人的道不一样：从不足的拿走，加给有余的。谁能把自己的余给天下？只有有道的人。

老子把不公平平平地说出来，这比多数安慰做得多：人的道从穷人拿走给富人。他没有说这公平。他说天的道不一样，而一个人可以在自己小小的经济里选择练哪一种道。苦涩是诚实的，它有用处，如果它变成你自己摆出拉弓姿势的理由：在你说得上话的地方把高的一端压下来，在你做得到的地方把低的一端擡起来。
zh_hans.reminder: 人的道不公平；你仍然可以反过来拉这张弓。
zh_hans.acting: 这星期给一个比你少的人一个小时、一项本事、或一次引介。

lines: 天下莫柔弱於水而攻堅強者
chapters.translation_en:
There is nothing in the world more soft and weak than water, and yet for attacking things that are firm and strong there is nothing that can take precedence of it;--for there is nothing (so effectual) for which it can be changed.
Every one in the world knows that the soft overcomes the hard, and the weak the strong, but no one is able to carry it out in practice.
 Therefore a sage has said,
 'He who accepts his state's reproach,
 Is hailed therefore its altars' lord;
 To him who bears men's direful woes
 They all the name of King accord.'
Words that are strictly true seem to be paradoxical.

en.plain: You feel like the softest person in a hard place, at work or in the family, and it seems like a weakness.
en.story:
Nothing in the world is softer or weaker than water, yet nothing is better at attacking the hard and strong, and nothing can replace it. The weak overcomes the strong, the soft overcomes the hard; everyone knows this and no one practises it. So the sage says: who takes on the state's dirt is its master; who takes on the state's misfortune is its king. Straight words seem to say the reverse.

Being the soft person in a hard place is the chapter's exact subject, and it does not call it a weakness. It calls it water, and it points out that water is the one thing the hard cannot resist over time, because it does not compete on hardness. The second half is stranger: the one who takes on the dirt is the master. The person who absorbs what the hard place produces, the tension, the mess, is doing the work that holds the place together, whether or not the place notices.
en.reminder: Water does not compete on hardness, and the stone still wears.
en.acting: Do the soft thing once today in the hard place, without apology, and let it stand.

zh_hant.plain: 你覺得自己是硬地方裡最軟的人，公司裡或家裡，這看起來像弱點。
zh_hant.story:
天下沒有比水更柔弱的東西，卻沒有東西比它更能攻堅強，沒有東西能取代它。弱勝過強，柔勝過剛；人人都知道，沒有人做得到。所以聖人說：承受國家的污垢的，是它的主人；承受國家的災禍的，是它的王。正話聽起來像反話。

在硬地方當軟的人，正是這一章的主題，而它沒有叫這個弱點。它叫它水，並指出水是唯一硬的東西長久抵擋不了的，因為它不在硬上面競爭。後半更奇怪：承受污垢的，是主人。吸收硬地方產生的東西、緊繃、混亂的那個人，做的是把那個地方撐在一起的工作，不管那個地方有沒有注意到。
zh_hant.reminder: 水不在硬上面競爭，石頭照樣磨損。
zh_hant.acting: 今天在那個硬地方做一次軟的事，不道歉，讓它站著。

zh_hans.plain: 你觉得自己是硬地方里最软的人，公司里或家里，这看起来像弱点。
zh_hans.story:
天下没有比水更柔弱的东西，却没有东西比它更能攻坚强，没有东西能取代它。弱胜过强，柔胜过刚；人人都知道，没有人做得到。所以圣人说：承受国家的污垢的，是它的主人；承受国家的灾祸的，是它的王。正话听起来像反话。

在硬地方当软的人，正是这一章的主题，而它没有叫这个弱点。它叫它水，并指出水是唯一硬的东西长久抵挡不了的，因为它不在硬上面竞争。后半更奇怪：承受污垢的，是主人。吸收硬地方产生的东西、紧绷、混乱的那个人，做的是把那个地方撑在一起的工作，不管那个地方有没有注意到。
zh_hans.reminder: 水不在硬上面竞争，石头照样磨损。
zh_hans.acting: 今天在那个硬地方做一次软的事，不道歉，让它站着。

chapters.translation_en:
When a reconciliation is effected (between two parties) after a great animosity, there is sure to be a grudge remaining (in the mind of the one who was wrong). And how can this be beneficial (to the other)?
Therefore (to guard against this), the sage keeps the left-hand portion of the record of the engagement, and does not insist on the (speedy) fulfilment of it by the other party. (So), he who has the attributes (of the Tao) regards (only) the conditions of the engagement, while he who has not those attributes regards only the conditions favourable to himself.
In the Way of Heaven, there is no partiality of love; it is always on the side of the good man.

en.plain: A debt or a grievance between you and someone close has been settled, and the resentment has not gone with it.
en.story:
When a great resentment is reconciled, some resentment remains; how can that be called good? So the sage holds the debtor's half of the contract and does not press for payment. One with virtue keeps the contract; one without virtue keeps the tally. The way of heaven has no favourites, and it always sides with the good person.

The chapter knows something about settlements: the money can be repaid and the resentment stay. Its remedy is the image of the two halves of a contract tally. The sage holds their own half and does not go around demanding the other. In practice this means the settled thing is treated as settled, with no reminders, no ledger kept, no reference to it in the next argument. The residue fades when it is given nothing to feed on, and that is the only way it fades.
en.reminder: Keep your half of the tally; stop keeping the score.
en.acting: Say nothing about the settled matter for a month, and notice how the residue behaves when unfed.

zh_hant.plain: 你和親近的人之間的一筆債或一件怨已經了結，怨恨卻沒有跟著走。
zh_hant.story:
大的怨被調解了，還會剩下一些怨；這怎麼能算好？所以聖人拿著債務契約的自己那一半，不去逼人償還。有德的人守契約；沒有德的人記帳。天的道沒有偏愛，總是站在善人那一邊。

這一章懂得一件關於了結的事：錢可以還了，怨還留著。它的藥方是契約的兩半的畫面。聖人拿著自己的那一半，不去到處要另一半。實際上這表示已經了結的事就當它了結了，不提醒，不記帳，下一次爭執時不再提。剩下的怨在什麼都不給它吃的時候消退，而那是它唯一會消退的方式。
zh_hant.reminder: 拿著自己那一半契約；不再記分。
zh_hant.acting: 一個月不提那件已經了結的事，注意剩下的怨在沒有東西吃的時候怎麼樣。

zh_hans.plain: 你和亲近的人之间的一笔债或一件怨已经了结，怨恨却没有跟着走。
zh_hans.story:
大的怨被调解了，还会剩下一些怨；这怎么能算好？所以圣人拿着债务契约的自己那一半，不去逼人偿还。有德的人守契约；没有德的人记帐。天的道没有偏爱，总是站在善人那一边。

这一章懂得一件关于了结的事：钱可以还了，怨还留着。它的药方是契约的两半的画面。圣人拿着自己的那一半，不去到处要另一半。实际上这表示已经了结的事就当它了结了，不提醒，不记帐，下一次争执时不再提。剩下的怨在什么都不给它吃的时候消退，而那是它唯一会消退的方式。
zh_hans.reminder: 拿着自己那一半契约；不再记分。
zh_hans.acting: 一个月不提那件已经了结的事，注意剩下的怨在没有东西吃的时候怎么样。

lines: 使人復結繩而用之甘其食
鄰國相望雞犬之聲相聞
chapters.translation_en:
In a little state with a small population, I would so order it, that, though there were individuals with the abilities of ten or a hundred men, there should be no employment of them; I would make the people, while looking on death as a grievous thing, yet not remove elsewhere (to avoid it).
Though they had boats and carriages, they should have no occasion to ride in them; though they had buff coats and sharp weapons, they should have no occasion to don or use them.
I would make the people return to the use of knotted cords (instead of the written characters).
They should think their (coarse) food sweet; their (plain) clothes beautiful; their (poor) dwellings places of rest; and their common (simple) ways sources of enjoyment.
There should be a neighbouring state within sight, and the voices of the fowls and dogs should be heard all the way from it to us, but I would make the people to old age, even to death, not have any intercourse with it.

en.plain: You dream of a smaller life, fewer things, fewer obligations, and it seems unrealistic in this city.
en.story:
A small state with few people, where tools that do the work of tens are not used, where people take death seriously and do not travel far, where boats and carts have no passengers and weapons are not displayed, where people knot cords again instead of writing, find their food sweet, their clothes fine, their homes secure, their customs pleasing; where the next village is within earshot of dogs and cocks, and people grow old and die without ever visiting it.

The chapter is Laozi's picture of enough, and it is not a policy; it is a description of a Sunday. Food that tastes sweet because it was cooked at home. A flat that feels secure because nobody is planning to leave it. A neighbourhood walked rather than driven through. None of it requires leaving the city or the job. It requires choosing, some days, to stay within earshot of the dogs. The small life is not a place to move to. It is a day that can be had this week.
en.reminder: The small life is a day, not a place.
en.acting: Spend one day this week within walking distance of home, with no plan that needs a car or a screen.

zh_hant.plain: 你夢想一種小的生活，東西少一點、義務少一點，在這座城市裡它看起來不切實際。
zh_hant.story:
小國寡民，做十人百人事的器具不用，人民看重死而不遠行，有船和車卻沒有人搭，兵器不陳列，人回到結繩記事，覺得食物甜、衣服美、住處安、風俗好；隔壁的村子雞犬相聞，人們到老死都不相往來。

這一章是老子畫的「夠了」的樣子，它不是一項政策；它描述的是一個星期天。因為在家煮所以嚐起來甜的食物。因為沒有人計畫離開所以覺得安穩的房子。用走的而不是開車穿過的街區。這些都不需要離開城市或工作。它需要的是在某些日子選擇留在雞犬相聞的範圍裡。小的生活不是一個要搬去的地方。它是這星期就能有的一天。
zh_hant.reminder: 小的生活是一天，不是一個地方。
zh_hant.acting: 這星期用一天待在走路到得了的範圍裡，不做任何需要車或螢幕的計畫。

zh_hans.plain: 你梦想一种小的生活，东西少一点、义务少一点，在这座城市里它看起来不切实际。
zh_hans.story:
小国寡民，做十人百人事的器具不用，人民看重死而不远行，有船和车却没有人搭，兵器不陈列，人回到结绳记事，觉得食物甜、衣服美、住处安、风俗好；隔壁的村子鸡犬相闻，人们到老死都不相往来。

这一章是老子画的「够了」的样子，它不是一项政策；它描述的是一个星期天。因为在家煮所以尝起来甜的食物。因为没有人计划离开所以觉得安稳的房子。用走的而不是开车穿过的街区。这些都不需要离开城市或工作。它需要的是在某些日子选择留在鸡犬相闻的范围里。小的生活不是一个要搬去的地方。它是这星期就能有的一天。
zh_hans.reminder: 小的生活是一天，不是一个地方。
zh_hans.acting: 这星期用一天待在走路到得了的范围里，不做任何需要车或屏幕的计划。

lines: 唐國子博士兼太子中允贈齊
州刺史吳縣開國男陸德明撰
文帝徵之不至自至河上責之
文帝改容謝之於是授漢文以
其後談論者莫不宗尚玄言
唯王輔嗣妙得虛無之旨
吾將鎮之以無名之樸夫亦將
chapters.translation_en:
Sincere words are not fine; fine words are not sincere. Those who are skilled (in the Tao) do not dispute (about it); the disputatious are not skilled in it. Those who know (the Tao) are not extensively learned; the extensively learned do not know it.
The sage does not accumulate (for himself). The more that he expends for others, the more does he possess of his own; the more that he gives to others, the more does he have himself.
With all the sharpness of the Way of Heaven, it injures not; with all the doing in the way of the sage he does not strive.

en.plain: You have been giving, time, money, help, and you are afraid it leaves you with less.
en.story:
True words are not fine; fine words are not true. The good do not argue; those who argue are not good. Those who know are not learned; the learned do not know. The sage does not hoard: the more he does for others, the more he has; the more he gives, the more is his. The way of heaven benefits and does not harm; the way of the sage acts and does not contend.

The last chapter ends with the arithmetic of giving, and it is the opposite of a bank's. The more the sage gives, the more is his. This is not a promise that money returns; it is an observation about what giving does to the giver, which is to leave them with more of the thing that was given: more time that felt like time, more help that made them capable. The fear of being left with less is honest. Check it against the evidence of the last year: what did the giving actually leave you with?
en.reminder: The more given, the more is yours; check it against last year.
en.acting: Give one small thing today and, this evening, write down what it left you with.

zh_hant.plain: 你一直在給，時間、錢、幫助，你怕它讓你剩下的更少。
zh_hant.story:
真的話不漂亮；漂亮的話不真。善的人不辯；辯的人不善。知道的人不博；博的人不知道。聖人不囤積：越為別人做，自己越有；越給人，自己越多。天的道，利而不害；聖人的道，做而不爭。

最後一章以「給」的算術結尾，它和銀行的相反。聖人給得越多，自己越多。這不是錢會回來的承諾；這是關於給對給的人做了什麼的觀察，它讓人剩下更多被給出去的那樣東西：更多感覺像時間的時間，更多讓自己變得有能力的幫助。怕剩下更少是誠實的。拿過去一年的證據來對照：給，到底讓你剩下了什麼？
zh_hant.reminder: 給得越多，自己越多；拿去年來對照。
zh_hant.acting: 今天給一樣小東西，晚上寫下它讓你剩下了什麼。

zh_hans.plain: 你一直在给，时间、钱、帮助，你怕它让你剩下的更少。
zh_hans.story:
真的话不漂亮；漂亮的话不真。善的人不辩；辩的人不善。知道的人不博；博的人不知道。圣人不囤积：越为别人做，自己越有；越给人，自己越多。天的道，利而不害；圣人的道，做而不争。

最后一章以「给」的算术结尾，它和银行的相反。圣人给得越多，自己越多。这不是钱会回来的承诺；这是关于给对给的人做了什么的观察，它让人剩下更多被给出去的那样东西：更多感觉像时间的时间，更多让自己变得有能力的帮助。怕剩下更少是诚实的。拿过去一年的证据来对照：给，到底让你剩下了什么？
zh_hans.reminder: 给得越多，自己越多；拿去年来对照。
zh_hans.acting: 今天给一样小东西，晚上写下它让你剩下了什么。
